title: Five-year butterfly persistence deficits appeared in both time directions in British records from 1990 to 2019
abstract: We tested whether low persistence after arrival identifies a slow establishment phase that could limit community warming. We used British butterfly site indices through 2024. Positive records after five zero years were matched to established records of the same species and year, with similar initial abundance, transect length and location. We followed outcomes for five years. In 1990-2004 and 2005-2019, 198 and 76 forward entries had persistence deficits of 32.4 and 29.1 percentage points. The same analysis with time reversed gave deficits of 35.2 and 30.7 points in 175 and 80 records. Forward-minus-reversed persistence contrasts had conditional spatial ranges that included zero in both periods. An early abundance-direction contrast did not repeat clearly in the later period. Exact initial-index matching retained deficits in both directions. A constant-mean Gamma-Poisson model proves that these history rules can produce a deficit even after exact current-count matching and without an establishment phase. The model is a counterexample, not a fit. The contribution is a time-direction control and a reproducible test of the establishment interpretation. The findings do not show that establishment costs are absent or quantify their share of weak thermal tracking. Detection, habitat, selected follow-up, small spatial samples and reused controls limit inference. Raw data and record-level panels stay external; the bundle contains code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and retrieval instructions.

display.caption: Matched butterfly records had lower persistence and abundance in both time directions. The directional persistence contrasts were uncertain in both periods. A constant-mean model gives the same type of deficit after exact current-count matching. The model is not fitted to the butterfly data. citations.reason: Tests the interpretation of rare newcomers as a slow establishment phase. Does not challenge its measured community slopes or prove that establishment costs are absent.
Weak community thermal tracking motivates the process question.
Uses its frozen European thermal-index table only for a sensitivity check.
Related source-distance recovery study on UKBMS. Our test uses different cohorts and a time-direction control.
